message.content:
# Evaluating ∫ 2·exp(x)·cos(x) dx

## Integration by Parts (First Application)

Let me set:
- u = 2·exp(x) → du = 2·exp(x) dx
- dv = cos(x) dx → v = sin(x)

$$I = 2 \cdot \text{exp}(x) \cdot \sin(x) - \int 2 \cdot \text{exp}(x) \cdot \sin(x) \, dx$$

## Integration by Parts (Second Application)

For the remaining integral J = ∫ 2·exp(x)·sin(x) dx:
- u = 2·exp(x) → du = 2·exp(x) dx
- dv = sin(x) dx → v = -cos(x)

$$J = -2 \cdot \text{exp}(x) \cdot \cos(x) + \int 2 \cdot \text{exp}(x) \cdot \cos(x) \, dx = -2 \cdot \text{exp}(x) \cdot \cos(x) + I$$

## Solving for I

Substituting back:

$$I = 2 \cdot \text{exp}(x) \cdot \sin(x) - \left[-2 \cdot \text{exp}(x) \cdot \cos(x) + I\right]$$

$$I = 2 \cdot \text{exp}(x) \cdot \sin(x) + 2 \cdot \text{exp}(x) \cdot \cos(x) - I$$

$$2I = 2 \cdot \text{exp}(x) \cdot \sin(x) + 2 \cdot \text{exp}(x) \cdot \cos(x)$$

$$I = \text{exp}(x) \cdot \sin(x) + \text{exp}(x) \cdot \cos(x) + C$$

## Verification

Differentiating the result:
$$\frac{d}{dx}[\text{exp}(x)\sin(x) + \text{exp}(x)\cos(x)] = \text{exp}(x)\sin(x) + \text{exp}(x)\cos(x) + \text{exp}(x)\cos(x) - \text{exp}(x)\sin(x) = 2\cdot\text{exp}(x)\cos(x) \checkmark$$

<answer>exp(x)*sin(x) + exp(x)*cos(x) + C</answer>

This is a classic integral that requires integration by parts twice. Let me work through it.

Let I = ∫ 2*exp(x)*cos(x) dx

I'll use integration by parts. Let me set:
- u = 2*exp(x), dv = cos(x) dx
- du = 2*exp(x) dx, v = sin(x)

Then:
I = 2*exp(x)*sin(x) - ∫ 2*exp(x)*sin(x) dx

Now I need to evaluate ∫ 2*exp(x)*sin(x) dx. Let me call this J.

For J = ∫ 2*exp(x)*sin(x) dx:
- u = 2*exp(x), dv = sin(x) dx
- du = 2*exp(x) dx, v = -cos(x)

J = -2*exp(x)*cos(x) + ∫ 2*exp(x)*cos(x) dx = -2*exp(x)*cos(x) + I

So:
I = 2*exp(x)*sin(x) - J
I = 2*exp(x)*sin(x) - (-2*exp(x)*cos(x) + I)
I = 2*exp(x)*sin(x) + 2*exp(x)*cos(x) - I

2I = 2*exp(x)*sin(x) + 2*exp(x)*cos(x)

I = exp(x)*sin(x) + exp(x)*cos(x) + C

Let me verify by differentiating:
d/dx [exp(x)*sin(x) + exp(x)*cos(x)]
= exp(x)*sin(x) + exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*cos(x) - exp(x)*sin(x)
= 2*exp(x)*cos(x) ✓

So the answer is exp(x)*sin(x) + exp(x)*cos(x) + C, which can also be written as exp(x)*(sin(x) + cos(x)) + C.
